people.john-vision.role: John, who writes down what he hears and sees
people.john-vision.relations: He calls the readers his brothers. He shares their oppression, Kingdom, and perseverance in Christ Jesus.
people.john-vision.meaning: John is on the isle of Patmos. He hears a loud voice behind him and sees one like a son of man. John falls at his feet like a dead man. He is told to write what he sees and send it to seven assemblies. At the end he falls to worship an angel, who tells him to worship God.
people.jesus.role: Faithful witness, firstborn of the dead, and ruler of kings
people.jesus.relations: John greets the seven assemblies from God, the seven Spirits, and Jesus Christ.
people.jesus.meaning: The book begins as the Revelation of Jesus Christ. A figure like a son of man says he was dead and is alive forever. He holds the keys of Death and of Hades. He speaks the messages to the seven assemblies. In the last chapter Jesus says he sent his angel and is coming soon.
people.balaam.role: Man who taught Balak to throw a stumbling block
people.balaam.relations: The message says Balaam taught Balak. It also names the children of Israel.
people.balaam.meaning: In the message to Pergamum, some there hold the teaching of Balaam. The message says he taught Balak how to make the children of Israel stumble. The teaching led them to eat things sacrificed to idols and to commit sexual immorality. The message gives no story of Balaam.
people.balak.role: Man Balaam taught to throw a stumbling block
people.balak.relations: The message says Balaam taught him. It also names the children of Israel.
people.balak.meaning: The message to Pergamum names Balak once. It says Balaam taught him to throw a stumbling block before the children of Israel. The message tells no other story about Balak.
people.david.role: King of old, named in titles of Jesus
people.david.relations: The key, the root, and the offspring are all called David’s.
people.david.meaning: David does nothing in Revelation. His name appears in titles. The one in Philadelphia’s message has the key of David. An elder calls the Lion of Judah the Root of David. Jesus calls himself the root and offspring of David.
people.moses.role: Servant of God, named in a song
people.moses.relations: Those who sing sing the song of Moses and the song of the Lamb.
people.moses.meaning: In chapter 15, John sees people standing beside a sea of glass. They sing the song of Moses, the servant of God. They also sing the song of the Lamb. The song praises the Lord God’s works and calls him King of the nations.
places.patmos.summary: In chapter 1, John says he was on the isle of Patmos. He was there because of God’s Word. There he hears a loud voice and sees seven lamp stands.
places.patmos.limits: The marker shows the island’s general location. The text gives no exact spot on it.
places.smyrna.summary: The message to Smyrna in chapter 2 names oppression and poverty. It warns that some will be thrown into prison. It says to be faithful to death and receive the crown of life.
places.smyrna.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location. The text names no meeting place.
places.pergamum.summary: The message to Pergamum in chapter 2 says the assembly holds to Christ’s name. It names Antipas, killed there. It warns of some who hold the teaching of Balaam.
places.pergamum.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location. The text names no meeting place.
places.thyatira.summary: The message to Thyatira in chapter 2 praises love, faith, service, and endurance. It warns that the assembly tolerates Jezebel, who calls herself a prophetess.
places.thyatira.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location. The text names no meeting place.
places.sardis.summary: The message to Sardis is in chapter 3. It says the assembly has a reputation of being alive but is dead. It says to wake up. A few there did not defile their garments.
places.sardis.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location. The text names no meeting place.
places.philadelphia.summary: The message to Philadelphia is in chapter 3. It says the assembly has little power but kept the word. It sets an open door before them and tells them to hold firmly.
places.philadelphia.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location. The text names no meeting place.
places.ephesus.summary: The message to Ephesus in chapter 2 praises toil, perseverance, and testing of false apostles. It says the assembly left its first love. It tells them to repent.
places.ephesus.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location. The text names no meeting place.
places.laodicea.summary: The message to Laodicea in chapter 3 says the assembly is neither cold nor hot. They say they are rich and need nothing. It tells them to repent and says, “I stand at the door and knock.”
places.laodicea.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location. The text names no meeting place.
sources.web.summary: The full text of Revelation is the main text for the close readings.
sources.web.limits: John is the named visionary. The text does not tie him to the apostle or the Gospel writer. Authorship, dates, Greek forms, and the exact opponents were not checked independently. The full meaning of its symbols was not checked either. Modern weapon or technology readings and any dated schedule of predictions were not checked. Heavenly and symbolic cities have no coordinates.
sources.cfm-nt-2023-50.summary: The lesson links the living Christ, counsel to each assembly, and the Lamb’s worthiness.
sources.cfm-nt-2023-50.limits: The lesson’s uses are Church teaching. Linked full talks, videos, Restoration passages, and reference entries were not reviewed independently. Historical descriptions of sealing practices were not reviewed either. Coverage follows what the lesson discusses, not its broad title.

sources.carey-revelation.summary: Carey reads the city coming down as a renewal of shared life, not an escape.
sources.carey-revelation.limits: This is Carey’s own reading. His claims about ancient marriage, Greek forms, and wider Jewish writings were not checked independently. His claims about empire and modern uses were not checked either. His wider comparison with chapter 22 does not add to the commentary coverage selected here.
sources.net-patmos.summary: The place description and coordinates give a general location for the island.
sources.net-patmos.limits: Only the place description and coordinates were checked. Older population figures, ethnic accusations, word origins, and archaeology were not checked independently. Religious customs and exile traditions were not checked either. The marker shows no exact building and does not confirm a vision.

chapters.*.mapNote: Markers show the seven addressed cities and the island of Patmos. Heavenly and symbolic settings have no marker.
chapters.*.routeEvidence: John lists the seven cities in order but names no travel route. The map draws none.
